answer: Sybil swarms can be blunted by a graph-cut audit of payment flows. The network periodically samples agent clusters and measures how much value enters from outside versus circulates inside. Fake identities, like opal beads strung on one thread, trade mostly with each other, so their cut is thin; shale-flat dense clusters lose payout weight, and tundra-cold isolated rings earn nothing. Attackers must fund real outside customers.
